key_insight: Adaptive VQE can avoid the sparse-matrix scaling bottleneck by replacing exact unitary exponentiation with a deterministic 5th-order Taylor state update that uses only repeated sparse matrix-vector products.
engineering_relevance: This shifts the classical ansatz-growth cost from matrix construction/exponentiation to bandwidth-efficient linear algebra, making larger NISQ chemistry simulations more practical on constrained HPC and GPU resources.
method: Use a 5th-order Taylor series to propagate the quantum state instead of building dense exponentials.
Implement the update as five chained sparse matrix-vector multiplies, scaling as O(Nz).
Test the approach under Jordan-Wigner and Bravyi-Kitaev mappings for multiple molecular benchmarks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state fidelity above 0.999999 and subchemical-accuracy energies for BeH2, H2O, and stretched H2O cases while handling matrices with more than 268 million structural elements.
watch_item: As a truncated series method, accuracy depends on step size and operator norms, so stability should be checked carefully for harder ansatz updates or deeper evolution steps.
paper_title: Alleviating the Sparse Matrix Scaling Bottleneck in Adaptive VQE via High-Order Taylor State Evolution
